name: dullahan

attributes.attribute: headless horseman who carried news of impending death

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The dullahan, also written dulachan, is the headless horseman of Irish tradition. Some accounts make him the driver of the Death Coach. Others describe a phantom riding a horse that itself lost its head. The dullahan is a masculine and lesser-known form of the Banshee, the wailing fairy that predicted death. He carried news of impending death to anyone who saw him pass. A flick of his whip could strike out their eyes.
